name: Schengen short-stay visa (Category C)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires showing you'll leave the Schengen area at the end of your visit.
This requires showing sufficient funds for the visit and return journey.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of sufficient funds and intent to leave

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: valid throughout the Schengen area, not just Spain; cannot be used to establish residence

sources.title: Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores — Schengen short-stay visa

notes: Fee €90 adults / €45 children 6-11 / free under 6 — same base figure as Germany's and Portugal's Schengen visitor routes, all implementing the same EU Visa Code (Reg. (CE) 810/2009). Special reduced reciprocity rates apply for some nationalities, and some (e.g. Mexican nationals) are entirely visa-exempt — a genuinely more varied fee/exemption landscape than the other three Schengen visitor routes in this dataset described so far, worth surfacing in a comparison view. ETIAS (€7, valid 3 years) is expected to become mandatory for visa-exempt travellers during 2026 but was NOT yet in force at this verification date — flagged as imminent rather than current, same treatment as Portugal's ETIAS note.
